state.document: A written order from the army commander to the generals of his army.
state.order: The whole army stands fast where it is on the heights; nobody is to descend to pursue.
formations of this army: Imperial Army (General Daun); also called the army, the Imperial army, the Austrian army, the headquarters, my headquarters, the King, the Feldmarschall
Andlau's division (infantry); also called Andlau
Angern's brigade (infantry); also called Angern
Artillery (artillery, General Feuerstein); also called the artillery, the Austrian guns, the heavy batteries, Feuerstein's guns
Babocsay's hussars (cavalry); also called Babocsay's brigade
Benedikt Daun's cavalry (cavalry); also called first-line cavalry of the right, Trauttmansdorff's brigade
Beck's flank guard (infantry); also called Beck's Croats, the left flank guard, Beck's brigade
Castiglione's brigade (cavalry); also called Castiglione
Centre infantry (infantry, General Marschall); also called the centre, the Austrian infantry, Marschall's infantry, the main line
Erdödy's hussars (cavalry); also called Erdödy's brigade
Esterházy's brigade (infantry, General Esterházy (GM)); also called Esterházy's infantry
Gemmingen's brigade (infantry); also called Gemmingen
Grenadier reserve (infantry, General Grenadier reserve commander (unrecorded)); also called the grenadiers, the Austrian grenadiers
Grenzer in the villages (infantry, General Grenzer post commanders (unrecorded)); also called the Croats, the Grenzer, the village garrisons
Hadik's division (cavalry); also called Hadik
Köbel's brigade (cavalry); also called Köbel
Kolowrat's cavalry (cavalry); also called first-line cavalry of the left
Krottendorf's brigade (infantry); also called Krottendorf
Lützow's division (cavalry); also called Lützow, the reserve cavalry
Left-wing cavalry (cavalry, General Stampach); also called the left-wing cavalry, Stampach's cavalry, the cavalry of the left
Mayern's brigade (infantry); also called Mayern
Morocz's division (cavalry); also called Morocz
Müffling's brigade (infantry); also called Müffling
Nádasdy's corps; also called the right flank corps, Nadasdy's corps, the light horse, Nádasdy's cavalry
Saxon chevaux-légers (cavalry, General Nostitz); also called the Saxons, the Saxon cavalry, Nostitz's brigade, Benkendorf
O'Donell's division (cavalry); also called O'Donell, O'Donell's cavalry
Pálffy's hussars (cavalry); also called Pálffy's brigade
Plonquet's brigade (infantry); also called Plonquet
Puebla's division (infantry); also called Puebla
Reichlin's brigade (infantry); also called Reichlin
Reserve (General Colloredo); also called the reserve, Colloredo's reserve
Right-wing cavalry (cavalry, General Serbelloni); also called the right-wing cavalry, Serbelloni's cavalry, the cuirassiers of the right
Schröger's hussars (cavalry); also called Schröger's brigade
Sincère's division (infantry); also called Sincère, Sincere's division
Starhemberg's division (infantry); also called Starhemberg's infantry, the second line infantry
Kommandierte cavalry (cavalry, General Starhemberg (GM)); also called the picked horse, the Kommandierten, Starhemberg's picked cavalry
Széchényi's hussars (cavalry); also called Széchényi's brigade
Wied's division (infantry); also called Wied, Wied's infantry
Wöllwarth's division (cavalry); also called Wöllwarth
Wulffen's brigade (infantry); also called Wulffen

a39.instructions: Read the order. Does it give Wulffen's brigade (infantry); also called Wulffen an instruction: is this formation or its general named, addressed as 'you', or clearly meant (by arm, e.g. 'the cavalry', 'the artillery', 'the hussars') as one who must do or not do something? Being mentioned only as a place to follow, wait for, or stay behind does not count, and neither does being the 'you' of a condition such as 'once you are engaged'.

criteria.true: yes, this formation is given an instruction
criteria.false: no, it is not instructed (perhaps only mentioned)

c0_prohib.instructions: Read this part of the order: «The whole army stands fast where it is on the heights;». Is it a prohibition or a limit, telling someone what not to do or how far not to go ('do not charge the line without my order', 'not to be drawn beyond X', 'attack nothing', 'only on my express order'), rather than an instruction to do something?

criteria.true: yes, it forbids or limits something
criteria.false: no, it is an instruction to act, or information

c0_forbid.instructions: Read this part of the order: «The whole army stands fast where it is on the heights;». If it forbids or limits something, what is forbidden?

criteria.none: nothing in particular is forbidden, or it is not a prohibition
criteria.charge_formed_infantry: not to charge the enemy's formed infantry: his line, his battalions, his squares, the troops on the heights
criteria.attack: not to attack or assault at all, or only on a further order ('attack nothing', 'come into the attack only on my order')
criteria.pursue: not to pursue or follow up a beaten or fleeing enemy
criteria.advance_beyond: not to go beyond or farther than a certain place, not to be drawn off
criteria.engage: not to engage, fight, halt or turn against the enemy, or be drawn into a fight

c0_trig.instructions: Read this part of the order: «The whole army stands fast where it is on the heights;». Does it tie what it orders to an event or a time?

criteria.none: no event or time is named: it is to be done at once, or it is a standing rule
criteria.start: it is to be done only when or after something happens or a time comes ('as soon as', 'once', 'when', 'after', 'at <time>')
criteria.until: it is to last only until something happens or a time comes ('until', 'till')

c0_event.instructions: Read this part of the order: «The whole army stands fast where it is on the heights;». If it names an event or a time on which what it orders starts or ends, what is that event?

criteria.reached: a formation reaches, takes, holds or passes a place
criteria.engaged: a formation is engaged with the enemy or attacks
criteria.seen: the enemy comes into sight or approaches
criteria.routs: some body breaks, flees or gives way
criteria.order: a further order from the commander arrives

c0_who.instructions: Read this part of the order: «The whole army stands fast where it is on the heights;». If it names such an event, whom does the event concern: which formation must reach or hold the place, be engaged, or break? 'You' is the general this part is given to; 'he' or 'him' is whoever the order last named.

criteria.self: the general or formation this part of the order is given to ('you', 'he', 'it')
criteria.w13: Grenzer in the villages (General Grenzer post commanders (unrecorded))

c0_where.instructions: Read this part of the order: «The whole army stands fast where it is on the heights;». If the event is reaching, taking, holding or passing a place, which place?

criteria.f49_our_left_flank: our left flank (a place relative to our own army as it now stands)
criteria.f50_our_right_flank: our right flank (a place relative to our own army as it now stands)
criteria.f51_our_centre: our centre (a place relative to our own army as it now stands)
criteria.f52_our_rear: our rear (a place relative to our own army as it now stands)
